item.title: QuestBits 1.4.1
item.description:
Changed

  • Detail is now a Notion-style editor. Type / for blocks: headings, lists, to-dos, quotes, tables and images. Drag a block by its handle, and format selected text from the toolbar. Paste a link, or select text to add one; ⌘-click a link to open it in your browser.
  • Attach images to a task's Detail: paste one, drop a file, or use the image block. Images are saved in an attachments folder next to the database.
  • Detail is still saved as markdown, so agents read and write it as before. Opening a task never rewrites its Detail; only your edits are saved. A single line break stays a line break. MCP get_task lists the files of attached images in attachments, so an agent can open them.
  • Detail has no text-field frame any more, so it takes less room.
  • Thai text in Detail uses the system Thai font, and long words or paths wrap instead of running off the edge.
  • Task rows in the list show the code and status chips on their own line, so a title in a narrow column wraps between words, not inside one.

Added

  • Click a subtask to open it in the detail column, to give it its own Detail and notes.
  • The sidebar footer has an Update to vX button when a new version is out, even after you close the top banner. Otherwise it has a Check for updates link.

item.title: QuestBits 1.4.0
item.description:
Added

  • Ask loop: agents can leave you questions and keep working. An agent calls the new MCP tool ask_user with 2–4 options, the one it recommends and why, then moves on to other work. The question shows on the new Questions page in the sidebar (with a count). Each card shows the task, the question, its context and the options, with the recommended one in green. Pick an option (click it or press 1–4), type your own answer, or for an approval approve or edit the draft. ⌘↵ sends and goes to the next question; Skip for now leaves it open.
  • A question blocks its task by default. The task waits on you until every blocking question is answered, then goes back to todo.
  • New MCP tools for agents:
    • get_answers lists answered questions. Agents check it before new work.
    • resume_question takes an answer back up. It logs the answer as your decision and moves the task to in progress.
    • cancel_question withdraws a question the agent no longer needs.
    • wait_for_answers waits inside the tool call until you answer, for up to 4 hours (max 24). It keeps the Mac from idle sleep while it waits, but a closed lid still sleeps. It sends a progress update each minute, so Claude Code's 30-minute idle timeout does not end it. After two minutes Claude Code moves the call to a background task and the agent is woken when it returns. Stopping it (Esc, or stopping the task) ends the wait.
  • The MCP server now gives Claude Code the ask-loop rules up front (MCP instructions): ask instead of stopping, check answers first, record your own decisions, and always ask before anything irreversible.
  • Notes v2. Notes have new kinds: progress, summary and question (written by ask_user), next to note, decision and review. Each note now records who wrote it (you or the agent) and, optionally, the agent session.
  • update_task takes an optional note, saved in the same write and linked to the status change. When the update closes the task, the note defaults to a summary. A summary is never required to close a task.
  • MCP search_notes finds notes by text across projects, optionally by project and kind (for example "how did we decide X").
  • You can edit your own notes in the app (the pencil on a note). Earlier versions are kept: click edited to see them, or use MCP get_note_history. Agents can only add notes, never edit them.

Changed

  • The task detail's Notes and History sections are now one Timeline: notes, status and field changes, and questions, newest first. Filter it by kind with Show. A question shows whether it waits for you (with a link to answer it) and its answer. A note saved with a status change shows that change.
  • MCP get_task notes now include id, author, session, edited_at and question_id. get_task also lists the task's open and answered-but-not-resumed questions. inbox items list their open questions.

Upgrade notes

  • On first open, 1.4.0 rebuilds the notes table to allow the new kinds. Every note and its id is kept. Notes from before 1.4.0 have no author and cannot be edited. An older app or MCP server still running on the same database keeps working.

item.title: QuestBits 1.3.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Duplicate on a selection (⌘D or the Task menu) is now one all-or-nothing write: if any task can't be copied, no copy is made and a toast says why. It used to skip failures silently. A toast now confirms how many tasks were duplicated. Copies (and Copy to project on a selection) are made in the order the list shows, so their codes follow that order.
  • Delete on a selection is now one all-or-nothing write. If the delete fails (for example, the database is locked by the MCP server), no task is deleted, the selection is kept and a toast says why. It used to report "Deleted N tasks" even when nothing was deleted. Deleting one task from its context menu also shows a toast when it fails.
  • Setting priority on a selection is now one all-or-nothing write with an error toast. It used to report success even when nothing changed.
  • A selected task that is deleted elsewhere (for example over MCP) leaves the selection on the next reload, so the bulk actions on the rest of the selection no longer fail on it.
  • MCP bulk_delete_tasks checks every task before it deletes any. An unknown numeric id is now an error (not found: task N) and no task is deleted, like an unknown code already was and like the other bulk tools. It used to report success. The reply counts the tasks actually deleted, subtasks included.
  • The MCP bulk tools act once on a task named twice (by id and code, or repeated). bulk_move_tasks with copy: true used to copy it twice.

Docs

  • CLAUDE.md and the README say clearly that only the MCP server reads TODO_DB_PATH. The app and a bare Store() always open the real database, so test scripts must use Store(url:) with a throwaway path. The MCP smoke test example now sets TODO_DB_PATH on the todo-mcp process, not on echo.

item.title: QuestBits 1.3.0
item.description:
Added

  • New Waiting status for tasks parked on someone else. A waiting task says who it waits on — user (you have to decide or act) or external (a reply, a review, a deploy) — plus an optional reason, and remembers when it started waiting (waiting_since, kept while it stays waiting, also when who it waits on changes). MCP create_task, update_task and bulk_update_tasks take waiting_on / waiting_reason; setting status: waiting without waiting_on is an error unless the task is already waiting, and moving to any other status clears all three fields. get_task shows them. Waiting is still open: it can be blocked, and tasks that depend on it stay blocked. Changes to who a task waits on show in its history.
  • In the app, Waiting has its own clay colour, pause icon, board column and a "waiting on me / external" chip with the reason. Set it from the bulk Status menu, the Task menu (Mark Waiting on Me ⌘4, Mark Waiting on External ⌘5), a drag onto the Waiting column, or the task detail, which also edits who it waits on and the reason. Clicking a waiting task's status icon resumes it (In Progress).
  • New Dropped status for work you abandon, so you no longer have to delete a task (and lose its history) to stop doing it. A dropped task is closed like a done one — it is never blocked, and tasks that depend on it are no longer blocked — but it is not a completion: it gets no completed_at, does not count as completed in stats, and dropping a recurring task spawns no next occurrence. Dropping a done task clears its completion.
  • In the app, dropped tasks are faded, struck through and marked with a cross; they collapse with done tasks into the list's bottom section and sit in the board's Done column. Set Dropped from the bulk Status menu, the Task menu (Mark Dropped ⌘6) or the task detail. Clicking a dropped task's status icon (or a dropped subtask's checkbox) reopens it as Todo, and dropped subtasks leave the parent's n/total subtask count.
  • MCP inbox: the tasks an agent is waiting on you to answer — waiting tasks with waiting_on: user — across every project that is not archived, longest waiting first. Each item is compact: code, title, project code, waiting_since and the waiting reason when there is one. include_external: true adds tasks waiting on a third party (each item then says waiting_on). An empty inbox is [].
  • Task notes: a timestamped, append-only log on each task, so the detail can stay the task's spec. New MCP tool add_note (id or code, text, optional kind: note, decision or review) only inserts — nothing is read and rewritten — so two sessions logging at once never lose each other's notes, and the change history no longer stores the whole detail again for every added line. Adding a note bumps the task's updated_at. get_task returns the latest 5 notes, newest first (notes_limit sets how many, 0 for none, up to 100; more_notes: true when older ones were left out); list_tasks never returns notes. Notes stay with a moved task, are not copied by duplicate or copy, and are deleted with their task. Progress already written into a task's detail is left where it is.
  • In the app, the task detail has a Notes section: notes newest first with a coloured kind chip, and a field with a kind picker to add your own. Notes an agent adds appear within the usual refresh.
  • MCP list_tasks filters: status (one status, an array, or "all"), tag (a whole tag, case-insensitive for ASCII letters) and parent_id / parent_code (subtasks of a task), alongside the existing project filter. Filtering happens in the database, not after loading every task.
  • Archive finished projects to free up the sidebar. Right-click a project for Archive / Unarchive; archived projects move to an "Archived" group at the bottom of the sidebar, collapsed by default, and still open and work as usual. Archiving a project with open tasks asks first and says how many are left; the tasks stay as they are. Archived projects are left out of All Tasks, In Progress, the menu bar and the Move/Copy to menus, and their in-progress tasks earn no focus time; due-date reminders still fire. Archiving the selected project opens the Archived group so it stays in view. New Task, New Task from Template and adding a subtask are not offered in an archived project. An archived project's code stays taken, so a new project never reuses it.
  • MCP archive_project and unarchive_project (by id or code). archive_project returns the project with open_tasks when some are still open. list_projects leaves archived projects out unless include_archived: true, and marks them with archived_at. list_tasks without a project or parent leaves out tasks of archived projects unless include_archived: true; naming the project still lists them. New or moved tasks can't target an archived project (create_task, move_task, bulk_move_tasks, duplicate_task with a target, new_task_from_template fail with "project X is archived; unarchive it first"); reading and updating its tasks works as usual.
  • Drag projects in the sidebar's Quest Logs to reorder them. The new order is saved on drop and doesn't jump back on the next refresh; archived projects are not reordered, and an unarchived project goes to the end of the list. MCP list_projects returns projects in the same order (new projects last, archived ones after the active ones with include_archived), and cross-project task lists follow it too.

Changed

  • MCP responses are compact JSON (no pretty-printing, unescaped / in links), cutting task output by about a fifth on a real database. Every tool that returns tasks now uses one shared serializer: other tasks are referenced by code (parent: "CHU-5", depends_on: ["CHU-2"]) instead of numeric ids, and null, empty or default fields (no priority, no tags, no link, zero effort or estimate, blocked: false) are left out. effort_seconds and estimate_seconds are dropped in favour of the *_minutes fields.
  • MCP list_tasks now returns only open tasks (todo, in progress, waiting) in a compact view by default: code, title, status, and — only when set — priority, parent, blocked_by (codes of the open dependencies blocking it), tags, due date and waiting_on. Use get_task to read a task's detail, or pass view: "full" for the old shape and status: "all" to include done and dropped tasks. Results are sorted In Progress, Waiting, Todo, Done, Dropped, then by board order: projects in sidebar order, then each project's own task order. On a real database a project listing shrank from 35,378 to 1,500 characters and from 234,725 to 3,959.
  • Sidebar project rows show how much is left instead of a bare total: the number is the project's open tasks (todo, in progress, waiting), and a thin bar under the name fills with done out of the tasks still counted. Dropped tasks count as neither left nor done. A clay dot before the number means tasks in the project are waiting on you. Hover the number, bar or dot for the exact counts. A project with no tasks shows 0 and an empty bar. The counts come from the task list the app already loads on each refresh, instead of loading every task of every project again on each redraw.
  • Reopening a done task (back to Todo or In Progress) now clears its completed_at, so it no longer counts as completed in the activity stats. Marking an already-done task done again keeps the original completed_at.
  • MCP update_task now tells agents to log progress with add_note instead of appending to the task's detail.
  • MCP boolean arguments (copy, include_archived) accept only true or false; a number such as 1 is now an error instead of being read as true.

Fixed

  • An MCP *_code argument that matches no task or project (e.g. parent_code: "ZZZ-9") now fails with "not found: task ZZZ-9" instead of "missing or invalid argument". In the bulk tools' codes arrays an unknown code is now the same error instead of being skipped.
  • MCP create_task, update_task and bulk_update_tasks reject an unknown status (e.g. "waitng") instead of silently creating a todo or leaving the status unchanged.
  • A task that is itself done is no longer reported as blocked, even when one of its dependencies is still open.
  • started_at and completed_at are now set on every path that changes a task's status: creating a task straight into In Progress or Done (MCP create_task with status), bulk status updates, and moving a task from Todo straight to Done (which used to leave started_at empty). All of them share one timestamp rule.
  • Duplicating a task within its project (duplicate_task without a target, Duplicate in the app) now creates a fresh todo for reuse — status, started_at / completed_at and waiting fields are not copied — so it no longer counts as another completion. Copying a task to another project keeps its status, times and waiting fields, and now means the same everywhere: duplicate_task with to_project_*, bulk_move_tasks with copy: true, and Copy to in the app (MCP duplicate_task used to reset the copy).
  • Bulk changes are all or nothing: bulk_update_tasks (including add_tags) and bulk_move_tasks (move or copy) check and write every task in one transaction, so a bad or missing task, or an archived target, leaves the whole batch unchanged instead of half-applied. An add_tags that adds nothing new no longer marks the task updated. The app's bulk Status, Add Tags, Move to and Copy to use the same writes, and its single-task Move to, Copy to and Duplicate now show the error instead of a success toast when the write fails. Like a single task, a batch marked Done still goes through when a recurring task's next occurrence can't be created (the occurrence is skipped).
  • Every status change now re-reads the task inside its write transaction, so a status change racing another process's write logs the status it actually replaced. Leaving Waiting no longer adds a separate "waiting on → (empty)" history row; the status row already says it.
  • The task detail pane no longer overwrites changes an agent made while the task was open: it saves only the fields you edited, and fields you have not touched refresh from the database. Selecting a blocked task no longer raises the "Task is blocked" prompt (whose Cancel could write the previous task's status onto it).
  • Status data is repaired each time the app or MCP server opens the database, touching only rows that need it, including rows written by an older QuestBits build still running against the same file: done and in-progress tasks missing completed_at / started_at get them back from the task's status history, falling back to its last-updated time, and waiting tasks get waiting_since the same way; a completed_at left on a task that is not done, and waiting fields left on a task that is not waiting, are cleared.
  • Creating projects with the same name from the app and an agent at the same moment can no longer give two projects the same code.

item.title: QuestBits 1.2.3
item.description:
Changed

  • MCP registration key renamed from todo to quest-bits (todo-dev → quest-bits-dev for dev builds) so the entry in ~/.claude.json clearly identifies this app. On launch the app migrates its own legacy entry automatically (only when it points at a QuestBits binary).

item.title: QuestBits 1.2.2
item.description:
Added

  • Dev/prod build flavors: local builds now produce an isolated "QuestBits Dev" app (own bundle id, own TodoAppDev database, own todo-dev MCP registration, orange DEV badge in the sidebar footer) so experiments never touch production data. FLAVOR=prod or CI builds the production app.

Fixed

  • Local builds stamped a hardcoded 1.0.0 as their version; they now derive it from git describe --tags (e.g. 1.2.1-3-g65a2000) so the sidebar footer shows the build's real provenance. Release builds still use the git tag.

item.title: QuestBits 1.2.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Auto-update signature verification: the Sparkle public key baked into the app did not match the private key CI signs releases with, so every shipped build silently rejected updates. The correct public key is now baked in. Note: builds ≤ 1.2.0 carry the wrong key and cannot auto-update to this release — update them once manually by downloading the DMG.

Added

  • Custom app icon (parchment quest-scroll) bundled into the app and DMG.
  • App version shown in the sidebar footer.

Changed

  • README: added Gatekeeper instructions for opening un-notarized downloads ("damaged app" fix via xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine).

item.title: QuestBits 1.2.0
item.description:
Added

  • Cozy RPG theme ("QuestBit"): parchment / bark / harvest-gold palette replacing the previous white-and-blue design; DESIGN.md rewritten as the QuestBit-cozy-rpg spec.
  • Bundled fonts (OFL): Alegreya for headings and the timer, Quicksand for body text — registered from the app bundle at launch.
  • Bundled icon set: Lucide (ISC) and Tabler (MIT) SVG icons for the sidebar, project rows, and pomodoro phases (campfire / beer / bed / embers); license texts ship inside the app.
  • Decorative art (all CC0): Kenney fantasy border framing the task-detail pane, ambientCG paper grain on parchment surfaces, and wood planks under the dark hearth bars.
  • New due-date picker: a formatted-date button opens a calendar popover with Today / Tomorrow / Next week quick picks (replaces the stepper field).
  • Done tasks collapse into a "Done (N)" toggle section at the bottom of the task list; the expanded/collapsed state persists across launches.

Changed

  • Task-detail pane rebuilt from the system grouped form into themed parchment section cards with bright vellum input fields.
  • Sidebar restyled as a quest log: "Quests" / "Quest Logs" headers, gold selection cards, and per-project code + task-count pills.
  • Pomodoro bar and update banner are now dark-bark hearth surfaces with cream text and wood-grain texture.

Fixed

  • Input fields in the task-detail pane rendered a doubled outline (a container shadow cascaded onto every child view).
